Claude's keep-untested keeps that diagnostic and is the safer choice under rule 4. Decide A3-016/A3-017/A3-020 together.

Either keep it untested as slice-9 groundwork, or delete it together with reviewerSourcePathAllowed and update DESIGN.md:554 and IMPLEMENTED-CAPABILITIES.md:300; if reviewer-source-reader.ts stays, the production-reach test then needs a kept-for entry naming 'slice 9 of the orchestration design' (tests/architecture/production-reach.test.ts:1-22), because this branch is its only caller. rows.evidence: The :636 then arm (status 'not_found') needs readQuerySubmission to return not_found, which the real reader does only when the QueryJob batch says missing (source-authority-reader.ts:184-185, :190) or the submission receipt lookupCommit says not_found (:206). loadCurrentQueryState has just loaded the same Job successfully (:629; the load at :598), and submitQueryJob writes the QueryJob, QueryRun, QueryJobSubmitted event and idempotency receipt in one commit (query-job-service.ts:727-776); the QueryJob codec requires the submission locator (query-record-codecs.ts:445-446). The store has no record delete/prune path (only DELETE FROM identity_claims, sqlite-record-store.ts:105; ports.ts:6 says it never drops snapshots). No concurrent writer can remove the job or receipt, so only a hand-edited/truncated store or a foreign writer reaches this label; U stands.

Claude's simplification (status === 'rejected' ? code+': '+reason : status) produces the same string for not_found (and drops the not_ready word with B-030); codex's keep-as-is is equivalent. rows.evidence: The :646 right operand (?? null) can only run when submitted.runRef is null or undefined. The only QueryJobSubmitted writer is query-job-service.ts:731-770 (encode only at :770), and newPendingQueryRecords always sets runRef to the full queryRunRef (query-run-recovery.ts:459-476). The event codec rejects a missing runRef key (jobIssues: undefined -> queryRunRefFromValue null -> 'job.runRef is not a complete QueryRunRef', query-record-codecs.ts:398-406, applied to the event at :508), so a decoded event's runRef is either a complete ref or null; for null, ?? null yields null, i.e. the same canonical JSON. The fallback therefore never changes the compared value and only an undefined key (which the codec refuses) would; D2 stands.
rows.proposal_note: Delete ?? null and compare canonicalJson(submitted.runRef) directly: for a foreign null runRef the comparison still differs from the current job and :650 throws as before. Only this expression changes; the type allows QueryRunRef | null (query-job.ts), so no cast is needed.

rows.evidence: The :650 then arm needs the stored submission event's initial Job to disagree with the current Job on queryJobId/projectId/workspaceId/goalId (:643-645), runRef (:646), submittedAt (:647), intent (:648) or the pending/no-answers/no-close initial state (:649). The event is written once from the submit draft (query-job-service.ts:727-770) and is immutable; later lifecycle steps spread the job and change only status/updatedAt/answers/closeReason (query-run-recovery.ts:562, and the machine uses the same job), and the reader already pins the exact event by the Job's own locator, eventId, identityKey/fingerprint and scope (source-authority-reader.ts:196-243). A mismatch therefore needs a hand-edited Job or event record or a foreign writer; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Keep untested (rule 4) is right, and the check is not fully redundant: the reader re-checks the event scope, eventId and identity/fingerprint but not goalId, runRef, submittedAt, intent or the initial pending/answers/close shape, which is the 'this is the original submission, not a later or foreign snapshot' invariant Claude names. Do not restore a test that rewrites the accepted submission.

rows.evidence: The :651 then arm needs the stored QueryJobSubmitted event to carry an agent actor, i.e. it is a read-time guard on a stored record. The only writer, submitQueryJob, admits only a Host principal with kind human or system (query-job-service.ts:220, :231-233) and copies that actor into the event (:743; encoded only at :770), so no platform writer produces the shape. But the event codec still accepts an agent actor (query-record-codecs.ts:191-199 isActorRef allows agent + RunRef), so a hand-edited or foreign event can carry one and pass the reader's eventId/identity/scope checks (source-authority-reader.ts:228-243). No production caller path, public step or real fault yields it, so refuted is false; the evidence nevertheless matches the U reading ('only a record written outside the platform's owners reaches it'), not D2's 'cannot arise'.
rows.proposal_note: The agreed deletion is valid for U, but it needs Claude's codec narrowing first: isActorRef (query-record-codecs.ts:191-199) must reject agent for this event, otherwise :652 no longer typechecks as human|system and the check cannot simply be dropped. Keeping it as that type narrowing and untested (rule 4) is the smaller diff. No test either way; do not add a test that forges an agent-actor event.
